designation: Arbre remarquable, classified by grand-ducal regulation (current list per the regulation of 31 January 2025). The designation attaches to the individual specimen.
attribution: Administration de la nature et des forets, Luxembourg
scope: 238 classified trees across the whole Grand Duchy, tree-level coordinates in WGS84.
caveat: Four things a run must know. (1) NO AGE FIELD and NO GIRTH FIELD. This register says protected and why, never how old or how thick, so every age here has to come from a second source or stay empty. (2) `essence` is often a GENUS, 'Tilia sp.' and 'Quercus sp.' both appear; ship the genus honestly and let the page ask the reader which one, never guess the species. (3) `interet` is the reason for designation (dendrologique, historique, paysager, ecologique and combinations) and it is the single most useful field here: it is the register itself saying why this tree was worth protecting, which is the closest thing to a story hook a register ever gives. (4) NO VITALITY FIELD, so whether a tree still stands is a per-tree check the register cannot do for us. The Luxembourgish Wikipedia mirrors this list ('Lescht vun de bemierkenswaerte Beem zu Letzebuerg') with individual articles citing the printed ANF monograph, and that mirror is where two removed trees were caught during the 2026-08-30 Luxembourg City pass: a copper beech in the City Museum courtyard removed in 2022, and one of the Parc Amelie sequoias felled 28 February 2026.
